original.task:
Add shop/cache.py with class TtlCache(ttl_seconds: float, max_size: int | None = None, clock=time.monotonic),
built on the LRU class in shop/lru.py. Methods: set(key, value), get(key, default=None), delete(key) -> bool,
"key in cache" and len(cache). An entry expires once clock() - stored_at >= ttl_seconds, so it is already gone
exactly at the ttl. set() on an existing key replaces the value and restarts its ttl; get() does not extend the
ttl. len() and "in" count only live entries. When max_size is set and a new key is inserted into a full cache,
expired entries are dropped first and only if it is still full is the least recently used live entry evicted;
both get() hits and set() count as use. Updating an existing key never evicts anything. A stored value of None
is a real value. delete() returns True only if a live entry was removed. The cache must be safe to use from many
threads, and instances must not share any state (no module-level mutable state). Add unit tests.

units.title: Create LRU store
units.spec: shop/lru.py contains an unbounded OrderedDict-backed LRU with recency operations. tests/test_lru.py covers it.
acceptance: shop/lru.py exposes LRU with exactly the listed methods.
All 8 tests (a)-(h) exist in tests/test_lru.py and pass.
units.objective: Provide the LRU class that TtlCache builds on.
steps: Create shop/lru.py with the docstring """A minimal least-recently-used ordered store (not thread-safe).""" and `from collections import OrderedDict`.
Define class LRU. __init__ sets self._data = OrderedDict().
__len__ returns len(self._data). __contains__(key) returns `key in self._data` and does not reorder.
get(key, default=None): if key in self._data, call self._data.move_to_end(key) and return self._data[key]. Otherwise return default.
peek(key, default=None): return self._data.get(key, default) without reordering.
put(key, value): set self._data[key] = value, then call self._data.move_to_end(key).
remove(key) -> bool: if key in self._data, delete it and return True. Otherwise return False.
pop_oldest(): return self._data.popitem(last=False). This returns a (key, value) tuple and raises KeyError when empty.
keys() -> list: return list(self._data.keys()), ordered least to most recently used.

Create tests/test_lru.py with `import unittest`, `from shop.lru import LRU`, and class LRUTests(unittest.TestCase) containing these tests: (a) test_put_get: put('a', 1); assertEqual(lru.get('a'), 1); assertEqual(lru.get('x', 'd'), 'd'). (b) test_get_marks_used: put('a', 1), put('b', 2), get('a'), then assertEqual(lru.pop_oldest(), ('b', 2)). (c) test_peek_does_not_reorder: put('a', 1), put('b', 2), assertEqual(lru.peek('a'), 1), then assertEqual(lru.pop_oldest(), ('a', 1)). (d) test_put_existing_replaces_and_marks_used: put('a', 1), put('b', 2), put('a', 3); assertEqual(lru.keys(), ['b', 'a']); assertEqual(lru.peek('a'), 3); assertEqual(len(lru), 2). (e) test_remove: put('a', 1); assertTrue(lru.remove('a')); assertFalse(lru.remove('a')); assertNotIn('a', lru). (f) test_pop_oldest_empty: with self.assertRaises(KeyError): LRU().pop_oldest(). (g) test_len_contains: put('a', 1), put('b', 2); assertEqual(len(lru), 2); assertIn('a', lru); assertNotIn('z', lru). (h) test_none_value: put('k', None); assertIsNone(lru.get('k', 'd')); assertIn('k', lru). Add the `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` footer.
constraints: Standard library only.
No module-level mutable state.

units.title: Create TtlCache and tests
units.spec: shop/cache.py contains TtlCache using a per-instance LRU and Lock, an injected clock, the expiry rule now - stored_at >= ttl, and expired-first then LRU eviction for new keys. tests/test_cache.py covers every requirement with a fake clock and includes a threaded smoke test.
acceptance: All 17 listed tests exist in tests/test_cache.py and pass.
The full suite passes, including the existing cart, pricing and storage tests and tests/test_lru.py.
shop/cache.py has no module-level mutable state; only _MISSING = object() is at module level.
units.objective: Implement the thread-safe TTL cache on top of LRU, with full unit tests.
steps: Create shop/cache.py with the docstring """A thread-safe cache whose entries expire after a fixed time-to-live.""", then `from __future__ import annotations`, `import threading`, `import time`, `from shop.lru import LRU`, and the constant `_MISSING = object()`.

class TtlCache, __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float, max_size: int | None = None, clock=time.monotonic): if ttl_seconds < 0, raise ValueError("ttl_seconds must be >= 0"). If max_size is not None and max_size < 1, raise ValueError("max_size must be >= 1"). Then set self._ttl = ttl_seconds, self._max_size = max_size, self._clock = clock, self._store = LRU(), self._lock = threading.Lock().
Private helper _expired(self, stored_at, now) -> bool: return now - stored_at >= self._ttl.
Private helper _purge_expired(self, now) -> None: for key in self._store.keys(): entry = self._store.peek(key); if self._expired(entry[1], now): self._store.remove(key).

Private helper _live_entry(self, key, now): entry = self._store.peek(key, _MISSING). If entry is _MISSING, return _MISSING. If self._expired(entry[1], now), call self._store.remove(key) and return _MISSING. Otherwise return entry. This does not reorder.

set(self, key, value) -> None: with self._lock: now = self._clock(). If key in self._store, call self._store.put(key, (value, now)) and return. Otherwise, if self._max_size is not None and len(self._store) >= self._max_size: call self._purge_expired(now), then `while len(self._store) >= self._max_size: self._store.pop_oldest()`. Finally call self._store.put(key, (value, now)).

get(self, key, default=None): with self._lock: now = self._clock(); entry = self._live_entry(key, now). If entry is _MISSING, return default. Otherwise call self._store.get(key) to mark it used and return entry[0]. Never modify stored_at.
delete(self, key) -> bool: with self._lock: now = self._clock(); entry = self._live_entry(key, now). If entry is _MISSING, return False. Otherwise call self._store.remove(key) and return True.
__contains__(self, key) -> bool: with self._lock: return self._live_entry(key, self._clock()) is not _MISSING.
__len__(self) -> int: with self._lock: self._purge_expired(self._clock()); return len(self._store).

Create tests/test_cache.py with `import threading`, `import unittest`, `from shop.cache import TtlCache`. Define class FakeClock: __init__ sets self.now = 0.0; __call__(self) returns self.now; advance(self, seconds) does self.now += seconds. Define class TtlCacheTests(unittest.TestCase). Every test creates its own clock = FakeClock() and passes clock=clock to TtlCache.

Add these tests to TtlCacheTests: (1) set/get basic (ttl=10): set('a', 1); get('a') == 1; get('x', 'd') == 'd'. (2) Expiry boundary with ttl=10: set('a', 1) at 0; clock.now = 9.999 -> get('a') == 1; clock.now = 10 -> get('a', 'd') == 'd', 'a' not in cache, len(cache) == 0. (3) set restarts the ttl (ttl=10): set('a', 1) at 0; advance 5; set('a', 2); advance 7 (now 12) -> get('a') == 2; advance 3 (now 15, 10 since re-set) -> 'a' not in cache. (4) get does not extend the ttl (ttl=10): set('a', 1) at 0; clock.now = 9 -> get('a') == 1; clock.now = 10 -> 'a' not in cache. (5) len and `in` ignore expired entries (ttl=10): set('a', 1) at 0; clock.now = 5; set('b', 2); clock.now = 10 -> len(cache) == 1, 'a' not in cache, 'b' in cache. (6) None value (ttl=10): set('k', None); assertIn('k', cache); assertIsNone(cache.get('k', 'd')). (7) delete (ttl=10): set('a', 1); assertTrue(delete('a')); 'a' not in cache; assertFalse(delete('a')); assertFalse(delete('missing')); set('b', 2); clock.now = 10; assertFalse(delete('b')). (8) LRU eviction (ttl=100, max_size=2): set a, set b, get('a'), set c -> 'b' not in cache, 'a' and 'c' in cache. (9) set counts as use (ttl=100, max_size=2): set a=1, set b=2, set a=3, set c=4 -> 'b' not in cache, get('a') == 3, 'c' in cache. (10) Updating never evicts (ttl=100, max_size=2): set a=1, set b=2, set a=3 -> len(cache) == 2, get('a') == 3, get('b') == 2. (11) Expired first (ttl=10, max_size=2): set a at 0; advance 1; set b; get('a'); advance 9.5 (now 10.5: a expired, b live); set c -> 'a' not in cache, 'b' in cache, 'c' in cache. (12) Instances do not share data: c1 = TtlCache(10, clock=clock), c2 = TtlCache(10, clock=clock); c1.set('a', 1) -> 'a' not in c2, len(c2) == 0. (13) Constructor validation: assertRaises(ValueError) for TtlCache(-1) and for TtlCache(10, max_size=0).

Add (14) the threaded smoke test: cache = TtlCache(ttl_seconds=60, max_size=50, clock=FakeClock()) with the clock never advanced; errors = [] (a list shared by all workers). Define a nested function `def worker():` whose body is `try:` around the whole loop `for i in range(2000): k = i % 100; cache.set(k, i); cache.get(k); cache.delete(i % 7); _ = k in cache`, followed by `except Exception as e: errors.append(e)`. Create threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(8)]; start each; join each. Then assertEqual(errors, []) and assertLessEqual(len(cache), 50).
Add (15) ttl == 0: cache = TtlCache(ttl_seconds=0, clock=clock); set('a', 1) -> get('a') is None (default), assertEqual(cache.get('a', 'd'), 'd'), 'a' not in cache, len(cache) == 0.
Add (16) re-set an expired key (ttl=10): set('a', 1) at 0; advance 10 (now 10, a expired); set('a', 2) -> get('a') == 2; clock.now = 19.999 -> get('a') == 2; clock.now = 20 -> 'a' not in cache.
Add (17) full cache with every entry expired (ttl=10, max_size=2): set a, set b at 0; advance 10; set c -> len(cache) == 1, 'c' in cache, 'a' not in cache, 'b' not in cache.
Add the `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` footer.
interfaces: def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float, max_size: int | None = None, clock=time.monotonic) -> None
constraints: Only private helpers touch internal state without acquiring the lock, and they are called only from public methods that hold it.
Call clock() exactly once per public call.
Every test, including the threaded test (14), passes a FakeClock instance as clock; never use time.sleep or the real clock in tests.
edge_cases: Exactly at the ttl means expired
A full cache where every entry is expired
Updating a key in a full cache

rules.text: Standard library only. Use unittest for tests.
No module-level mutable state. All state lives on the instance.
Time comes only from the injected clock.

dont_list: Don't use `>` for expiry. Use `now - stored_at >= ttl`.
Don't use None to detect a missing entry. Use _MISSING.
Don't call public methods (or acquire self._lock) from inside other locked methods or helpers.
Don't evict when updating an existing key.
Don't evict a live LRU entry before purging expired ones.
Don't compare pop_oldest() to a bare key; it returns a (key, value) tuple.
Don't modify existing shop/ modules or their tests.

facts.text: The task says TtlCache is built on 'the LRU class in shop/lru.py', but shop/lru.py is not in the repository. Only shop/__init__.py, cart.py, money.py, pricing.py and storage.py exist under shop/. The LRU class has to be created first.
The project uses only the standard library. Tests use unittest and run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.
Test files are named tests/test_<module>.py. Each has a unittest.TestCase subclass and an `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` footer. They import from the `shop.` package.
Project conventions: keep functions small, no module-level mutable state, take clocks as parameters, and add tests in tests/test_<module>.py.
tests/__init__.py exists, so tests is a package.
Modules start with a one-line docstring and use type hints in signatures.

assumptions: Because shop/lru.py does not exist, the plan creates it with a minimal, unbounded LRU ordering store. TtlCache adds TTL, capacity and locking on top of it.
The Python version supports `int | None` in annotations (3.10+), because the task signature uses it. `from __future__ import annotations` is added anyway for safety.
Argument validation is not specified. ttl_seconds < 0 and max_size < 1 raise ValueError. ttl_seconds == 0 is allowed and means every entry is expired immediately.

requirements.text: shop/cache.py defines class TtlCache(ttl_seconds: float, max_size: int | None = None, clock=time.monotonic), built on an LRU class in shop/lru.py.
Methods: set(key, value), get(key, default=None), delete(key) -> bool, __contains__, __len__.
An entry is expired when clock() - stored_at >= ttl_seconds, so it is already gone exactly at the ttl.
set() on an existing key replaces the value and restarts its ttl. get() does not extend the ttl.
len() and `in` count only live entries.

When max_size is set and a new key is inserted into a full cache, all expired entries are dropped first. Only if the cache is still full is the least recently used live entry evicted. Both get() hits and set() count as use.
Updating an existing key never evicts anything.
A stored value of None is a real value: `in` is True and get returns None rather than the default.
delete() returns True only if a live entry was removed.
The cache is safe to use from many threads.
Instances share no state and there is no module-level mutable state.
Add unit tests.

preserve: Existing modules shop/cart.py, money.py, pricing.py and storage.py and their tests stay unchanged and keep passing.
risks: Off-by-one at the ttl boundary: the check must use >=, not >.
Treating a None value as missing. A private sentinel object must be used instead.
Deadlock if a private helper acquires a non-reentrant lock while the caller already holds it.
Evicting on an update of an existing key, or evicting a live LRU entry while expired entries still exist.

architecture.summary: shop/lru.py provides LRU, an unbounded, non-thread-safe ordering store wrapping collections.OrderedDict (least recently used first). shop/cache.py provides TtlCache. It stores (value, stored_at) tuples in a per-instance LRU and guards every public method with a per-instance threading.Lock. It reads clock() once per public call, while holding the lock. Expiry, purging and eviction live in small private helpers that assume the lock is already held.

components.name: LRU
components.responsibility: Ordered key/value store with recency operations: get (marks used), peek (no reorder), put (insert/replace, marks used), remove, pop_oldest, keys, len, contains.

components.name: TtlCache
components.responsibility: Thread-safe TTL cache with optional max_size, built on LRU.

components.name: TtlCache tests
components.responsibility: Unit tests for TtlCache using a fake clock, including a multithreaded smoke test.

invariants: When max_size is set, len(self._store) <= max_size after every public call.
Each LRU value inside TtlCache is a (value, stored_at) tuple.
Every read or mutation of self._store happens while holding self._lock.
clock() is called at most once per public method call.
architecture.error_handling: The constructor raises ValueError if ttl_seconds < 0, or if max_size is not None and max_size < 1. All other operations do not raise for missing or expired keys. LRU.pop_oldest raises KeyError when empty, but TtlCache only calls it when the store is non-empty.
architecture.security: No module-level mutable state. The sentinel `_MISSING = object()` is an immutable identity marker and is allowed.
architecture.performance: get, set, delete and contains are O(1), except when inserting into a full cache: that does an O(n) purge of expired entries. len() also purges in O(n).

decisions.title: Create shop/lru.py because it is missing
decisions.decision: Create shop/lru.py containing class LRU, an unbounded OrderedDict wrapper with no capacity and no locking.
decisions.rationale: The task requires building on shop/lru.py, which does not exist. Keeping LRU free of capacity rules lets TtlCache apply its own rule: drop expired entries first, then evict the least recently used.
alternatives_rejected: Implementing TtlCache directly on OrderedDict (violates 'built on the LRU class').
Giving LRU its own max_size auto-eviction (it would evict live entries before expired ones).
constraints: LRU has no lock and no capacity.
LRU uses only collections.OrderedDict.

decisions.title: One per-instance threading.Lock
decisions.decision: TtlCache.__init__ creates self._lock = threading.Lock(). Each public method (set, get, delete, __contains__, __len__) wraps its whole body in `with self._lock:`. Private helpers never acquire the lock.
decisions.rationale: Simple, correct mutual exclusion. A non-reentrant lock is fine because helpers never re-acquire it.
alternatives_rejected: Locking inside LRU (double locking, harder to reason about)
constraints: Public methods must not call other public methods of the same instance.

decisions.title: Storage format and None handling
decisions.decision: Store the tuple (value, stored_at) in the LRU. Detect absence with the module constant `_MISSING = object()` passed as the default to LRU.peek.
decisions.rationale: None is a real value, so it cannot also signal absence.
alternatives_rejected: Using None as the absent marker
constraints: Never test `is None` to check presence.

decisions.title: Expiry semantics
decisions.decision: An entry is expired iff now - stored_at >= self._ttl. Expired entries found by get, delete or __contains__ are removed physically. len() purges all expired entries, then returns len(self._store). `in` does not count as use.
decisions.rationale: Matches the specification exactly. The spec names only get hits and set as use.
constraints: get() never changes stored_at.

decisions.title: set() behaviour
decisions.decision: If the key is physically present in the store (live or expired), overwrite it via put(key, (value, now)) and do no eviction. Otherwise, if max_size is set and the store is full, purge expired entries first, then call pop_oldest() while len >= max_size, then put.
decisions.rationale: Overwriting does not grow the store, so it never needs eviction. Re-setting an expired key behaves like a fresh insert with a new ttl.
alternatives_rejected: Evicting the LRU entry without purging expired ones first
constraints: Purge expired entries before any LRU eviction.

decisions.title: Constructor validation
decisions.decision: Raise ValueError if ttl_seconds < 0. Raise ValueError if max_size is not None and max_size < 1.
decisions.rationale: Prevents nonsensical configurations at low cost.
constraints: ttl_seconds == 0 is allowed.

(5) len and `in` ignore expired entries (ttl=10): set('a', 1) at 0; clock.now = 5; set('b', 2); clock.now = 10 -> len(cache) == 1, 'a' not in cache, 'b' in cache. (6) None value (ttl=10): set('k', None); assertIn('k', cache); assertIsNone(cache.get('k', 'd')). (7) delete (ttl=10): set('a', 1); assertTrue(delete('a')); 'a' not in cache; assertFalse(delete('a')); assertFalse(delete('missing')); set('b', 2); clock.now = 10; assertFalse(delete('b')). (8) LRU eviction (ttl=100, max_size=2): set a, set b, get('a'), set c -> 'b' not in cache, 'a' and 'c' in cache. (9) set counts as use (ttl=100, max_size=2): set a=1, set b=2, set a=3, set c=4 -> 'b' not in cache, get('a') == 3, 'c' in cache. (10) Updating never evicts (ttl=100, max_size=2): set a=1, set b=2, set a=3 -> len(cache) == 2, get('a') == 3, get('b') == 2. (11) Expired first (ttl=10, max_size=2): set a at 0; advance 1; set b; get('a'); advance 9.5 (now 10.5: a expired, b live); set c -> 'a' not in cache, 'b' in cache, 'c' in cache. (12) Instances do not share data: c1 = TtlCache(10, clock=clock), c2 = TtlCache(10, clock=clock); c1.set('a', 1) -> 'a' not in c2, len(c2) == 0. (13) Constructor validation: assertRaises(ValueError) for TtlCache(-1) and for TtlCache(10, max_size=0).

Add (14) the threaded smoke test: cache = TtlCache(ttl_seconds=60, max_size=50, clock=FakeClock()) with the clock never advanced; errors = [] (a list shared by all workers). Define a nested function `def worker():` whose body is `try:` around the whole loop `for i in range(2000): k = i % 100; cache.set(k, i); cache.get(k); cache.delete(i % 7); _ = k in cache`, followed by `except Exception as e: errors.append(e)`. Create threads = [threading.Thread(target=worker) for _ in range(8)]; start each; join each. Then assertEqual(errors, []) and assertLessEqual(len(cache), 50).
Add (15) ttl == 0: cache = TtlCache(ttl_seconds=0, clock=clock); set('a', 1) -> get('a') is None (default), assertEqual(cache.get('a', 'd'), 'd'), 'a' not in cache, len(cache) == 0.
Add (16) re-set an expired key (ttl=10): set('a', 1) at 0; advance 10 (now 10, a expired); set('a', 2) -> get('a') == 2; clock.now = 19.999 -> get('a') == 2; clock.now = 20 -> 'a' not in cache.
Add (17) full cache with every entry expired (ttl=10, max_size=2): set a, set b at 0; advance 10; set c -> len(cache) == 1, 'c' in cache, 'a' not in cache, 'b' not in cache.
Add the `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` footer.
interfaces: def __init__(self, ttl_seconds: float, max_size: int | None = None, clock=time.monotonic) -> None
constraints: Only private helpers touch internal state without acquiring the lock, and they are called only from public methods that hold it.
Call clock() exactly once per public call.
Every test, including the threaded test (14), passes a FakeClock instance as clock; never use time.sleep or the real clock in tests.
edge_cases: Exactly at the ttl means expired
A full cache where every entry is expired
Updating a key in a full cache

rules.text: Standard library only. Use unittest for tests.
No module-level mutable state. All state lives on the instance.
Time comes only from the injected clock.

dont_list: Don't use `>` for expiry. Use `now - stored_at >= ttl`.
Don't use None to detect a missing entry. Use _MISSING.
Don't call public methods (or acquire self._lock) from inside other locked methods or helpers.
Don't evict when updating an existing key.
Don't evict a live LRU entry before purging expired ones.
Don't compare pop_oldest() to a bare key; it returns a (key, value) tuple.
Don't modify existing shop/ modules or their tests.

facts.text: The task says TtlCache is built on 'the LRU class in shop/lru.py', but shop/lru.py is not in the repository. Only shop/__init__.py, cart.py, money.py, pricing.py and storage.py exist under shop/. The LRU class has to be created first.
The project uses only the standard library. Tests use unittest and run with `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`.
Test files are named tests/test_<module>.py. Each has a unittest.TestCase subclass and an `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()` footer. They import from the `shop.` package.
Project conventions: keep functions small, no module-level mutable state, take clocks as parameters, and add tests in tests/test_<module>.py.
tests/__init__.py exists, so tests is a package.
Modules start with a one-line docstring and use type hints in signatures.

assumptions: Because shop/lru.py does not exist, the plan creates it with a minimal, unbounded LRU ordering store. TtlCache adds TTL, capacity and locking on top of it.
The Python version supports `int | None` in annotations (3.10+), because the task signature uses it. `from __future__ import annotations` is added anyway for safety.
Argument validation is not specified. ttl_seconds < 0 and max_size < 1 raise ValueError. ttl_seconds == 0 is allowed and means every entry is expired immediately.

requirements.text: shop/cache.py defines class TtlCache(ttl_seconds: float, max_size: int | None = None, clock=time.monotonic), built on an LRU class in shop/lru.py.
Methods: set(key, value), get(key, default=None), delete(key) -> bool, __contains__, __len__.
An entry is expired when clock() - stored_at >= ttl_seconds, so it is already gone exactly at the ttl.
set() on an existing key replaces the value and restarts its ttl. get() does not extend the ttl.
len() and `in` count only live entries.

When max_size is set and a new key is inserted into a full cache, all expired entries are dropped first. Only if the cache is still full is the least recently used live entry evicted. Both get() hits and set() count as use.
Updating an existing key never evicts anything.
A stored value of None is a real value: `in` is True and get returns None rather than the default.
delete() returns True only if a live entry was removed.
The cache is safe to use from many threads.
Instances share no state and there is no module-level mutable state.
Add unit tests.

preserve: Existing modules shop/cart.py, money.py, pricing.py and storage.py and their tests stay unchanged and keep passing.
risks: Off-by-one at the ttl boundary: the check must use >=, not >.
Treating a None value as missing. A private sentinel object must be used instead.
Deadlock if a private helper acquires a non-reentrant lock while the caller already holds it.
Evicting on an update of an existing key, or evicting a live LRU entry while expired entries still exist.

architecture.summary: shop/lru.py provides LRU, an unbounded, non-thread-safe ordering store wrapping collections.OrderedDict (least recently used first). shop/cache.py provides TtlCache. It stores (value, stored_at) tuples in a per-instance LRU and guards every public method with a per-instance threading.Lock. It reads clock() once per public call, while holding the lock. Expiry, purging and eviction live in small private helpers that assume the lock is already held.

components.name: LRU
components.responsibility: Ordered key/value store with recency operations: get (marks used), peek (no reorder), put (insert/replace, marks used), remove, pop_oldest, keys, len, contains.

components.name: TtlCache
components.responsibility: Thread-safe TTL cache with optional max_size, built on LRU.

components.name: TtlCache tests
components.responsibility: Unit tests for TtlCache using a fake clock, including a multithreaded smoke test.

invariants: When max_size is set, len(self._store) <= max_size after every public call.
Each LRU value inside TtlCache is a (value, stored_at) tuple.
Every read or mutation of self._store happens while holding self._lock.
clock() is called at most once per public method call.
architecture.error_handling: The constructor raises ValueError if ttl_seconds < 0, or if max_size is not None and max_size < 1. All other operations do not raise for missing or expired keys. LRU.pop_oldest raises KeyError when empty, but TtlCache only calls it when the store is non-empty.
architecture.security: No module-level mutable state. The sentinel `_MISSING = object()` is an immutable identity marker and is allowed.
architecture.performance: get, set, delete and contains are O(1), except when inserting into a full cache: that does an O(n) purge of expired entries. len() also purges in O(n).

decisions.title: Create shop/lru.py because it is missing
decisions.decision: Create shop/lru.py containing class LRU, an unbounded OrderedDict wrapper with no capacity and no locking.
decisions.rationale: The task requires building on shop/lru.py, which does not exist. Keeping LRU free of capacity rules lets TtlCache apply its own rule: drop expired entries first, then evict the least recently used.
alternatives_rejected: Implementing TtlCache directly on OrderedDict (violates 'built on the LRU class').
Giving LRU its own max_size auto-eviction (it would evict live entries before expired ones).
constraints: LRU has no lock and no capacity.
LRU uses only collections.OrderedDict.

decisions.title: One per-instance threading.Lock
decisions.decision: TtlCache.__init__ creates self._lock = threading.Lock(). Each public method (set, get, delete, __contains__, __len__) wraps its whole body in `with self._lock:`. Private helpers never acquire the lock.
decisions.rationale: Simple, correct mutual exclusion. A non-reentrant lock is fine because helpers never re-acquire it.
alternatives_rejected: Locking inside LRU (double locking, harder to reason about)
constraints: Public methods must not call other public methods of the same instance.

decisions.title: Storage format and None handling
decisions.decision: Store the tuple (value, stored_at) in the LRU. Detect absence with the module constant `_MISSING = object()` passed as the default to LRU.peek.
decisions.rationale: None is a real value, so it cannot also signal absence.
alternatives_rejected: Using None as the absent marker
constraints: Never test `is None` to check presence.

decisions.title: Expiry semantics
decisions.decision: An entry is expired iff now - stored_at >= self._ttl. Expired entries found by get, delete or __contains__ are removed physically. len() purges all expired entries, then returns len(self._store). `in` does not count as use.
decisions.rationale: Matches the specification exactly. The spec names only get hits and set as use.
constraints: get() never changes stored_at.

decisions.title: set() behaviour
decisions.decision: If the key is physically present in the store (live or expired), overwrite it via put(key, (value, now)) and do no eviction. Otherwise, if max_size is set and the store is full, purge expired entries first, then call pop_oldest() while len >= max_size, then put.
decisions.rationale: Overwriting does not grow the store, so it never needs eviction. Re-setting an expired key behaves like a fresh insert with a new ttl.
alternatives_rejected: Evicting the LRU entry without purging expired ones first
constraints: Purge expired entries before any LRU eviction.

decisions.title: Constructor validation
decisions.decision: Raise ValueError if ttl_seconds < 0. Raise ValueError if max_size is not None and max_size < 1.
decisions.rationale: Prevents nonsensical configurations at low cost.
constraints: ttl_seconds == 0 is allowed.
